subject.title: feat(config): use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should OpenClaw preserve legacy numbered config backups during the timestamped-backup migration, or may the first upgraded maintenance run prune them as stale backups?
rationale: The requested change is useful and source-reproducible, but it changes persistent recovery artifacts and the open PR proposals disagree with the issue's suggested preserve-or-convert migration behavior.

options.title: Preserve legacy backups during migration
options.body: Keep .bak.1-.bak.4 as valid legacy recovery files until the cap can be enforced without silently deleting the only known-good backup.

options.title: Prune legacy backups on first maintenance
options.body: Treat numbered backups as obsolete orphans and rely on the new timestamped set going forward, accepting the upgrade recovery risk.

options.title: Defer naming change
options.body: Keep numeric rotation until a broader backup-location and retention design is decided with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20460.

recommendation.title: Preserve legacy backups during migration
recommendation.body: Keep .bak.1-.bak.4 as valid legacy recovery files until the cap can be enforced without silently deleting the only known-good backup.

likelyOwner.reason: Their commit introduced the current config backup rotation behavior, making them the strongest history-based routing candidate for the migration choice.
